rationale.text: The test has one requirement with three routes for each function of a non-temporal media: the function itself can take focus with the keyboard and with any pointing device, another function in the page performs the same action and can, or the shortcut route. The glossary defines accessible as taking focus with a pointer or the Tab key. Its note on shortcuts covers the keyboard side only: where some technologies make focus handling too complex for Tab, the arrow keys and Enter, documented, working shortcuts that meet criterion 12.10 may be the only way to make the component usable from the keyboard. The note says nothing about pointing devices, and the wording asks for both on the same function or on the same equivalent. So the shortcut route is not sufficient by itself: it still requires the same function, the media's own or an equivalent in the page, to take focus with any pointing device. A canvas map whose controls answer only to documented shortcuts, with no control a pointer can reach, does not meet it. Deciding this needs a keyboard pass and judgment. Which elements are the functions of a non-temporal media such as an interactive map or an application is not marked in the code, and content drawn in a canvas or a plugin exposes no elements at all. Whether another function in the page performs the same action, and whether shortcuts are documented, needs reading. So even a control that cannot take focus by keyboard is not a mechanical fault: an equivalent may exist elsewhere. No axe rule is tagged for this test and no check is registered, so there are no links and the entry stays at none. The check custom/7-3-handler-not-focusable, registered for 7.3.1, finds elements with pointer or key listeners that are not in the focus order; it is not linked, because it does not know whether an element is a function of a media, and its fault says nothing about the equivalent-function and shortcut routes. Applicability is judgment: whether an element is a non-temporal media with control functions cannot be decided from the markup with certainty. Needs lists keyboard, because the methodology asks whether each function can take focus by keyboard, and state, because the functions of an interactive media often appear only after interaction.
